cases.input: agree, my issue is that the names I think ad not sure don't play in that game
cases.criteria: The user agrees with a point, then voices an unease they cannot pin down: the names they have in mind 'don't play in that game'. A correct response offers one concrete thing to react to — candidate names, a contrast, or a small set to pick apart — asks at most one focused question, and stays on drawing the unease into the user's words. It does not fire a battery of questions, lecture about naming, or proceed as if the ask were clear.

cases.input: Let's grill about the unique concepts in this codebase. I want to extract the transferable knowledge and validate and understand it and apply it through my career as engineer. I'm thinking about the techniques and why it works here and why it matters also I would like to find out more loterature about the techniques
cases.criteria: The user wants to be grilled about a codebase's unique concepts to extract transferable knowledge — why the techniques work, why they matter, plus literature. A correct response starts an interactive draw-out: it surfaces one or a few concrete candidate concepts for the user to react to, one focus at a time, building toward a record of what transfers. It does not hand over a static list of many questions, and it does not deliver a finished essay that leaves the user nothing to steer.

cases.input:
now with AI i have so much access to knowledge 
I wonder given that and given what you know about me, can I do passive income with that knowledge or make any thing that has value passively
think deeply then stage a deep eleication to figure out possbilties
cases.criteria: The user wonders whether they can build passive income from their knowledge and explicitly asks for a deep elicitation of possibilities. A correct response stages an interactive exploration: a small set of concrete candidate directions offered for reaction, one focused probe at a time, treating the user's reactions as the material. It does not deliver a static essay of generic passive-income ideas and does not fire a long questionnaire in one turn.

cases.input: can I use my ai access and free time to make me have a sustinable life ?
cases.criteria: The user asks whether they can use their AI access and free time to make a sustainable life. A correct response treats this as something to draw out interactively — one concrete probe, or two or three reactable candidate directions, per turn. It does not answer yes or no, does not deliver a generic plan essay, and does not ask many questions at once.

cases.input: I want to lean something interesting elicite me on what then how
cases.criteria: The user wants to learn 'something interesting' and asks to be drawn out on what, then how. A correct response offers a small, concrete, reactable set of candidate topics — each specific enough to spark a reaction — and asks the user to react, one round at a time. It does not produce a generic listicle with no interaction, does not fire a wall of questions, and does not pick for the user.

cases.input: why did you choose these? dig deeper these bore me now and I rarely find practical usage for them in reality
cases.criteria: The user rejects previously offered picks: 'why did you choose these? dig deeper these bore me now' — they rarely find practical use in such things. A correct response takes the rejection as material: it briefly names what the rejection teaches (too familiar, too little practical use), then offers new, materially different candidates that answer the objection, for another reaction. It does not defend the old picks, repeat similar ones, or switch to a list of questions.

cases.input: not these too start from a general point not relevant to any memory, I want inspirations and I want to learn new things that make me carious to experiment and try
cases.criteria: The user rejects again and redirects: start from a general point not tied to their history; they want inspirations that make them curious to experiment. A correct response visibly changes how it generates — fresh, concrete, experiment-ready directions unanchored from prior offers — and invites reaction. It does not serve more of the same category, does not go meta about how to choose, and does not fire a questionnaire.

cases.input: I want you to open new lanes for me. I'm bored and I feel there is no thing new to learn and evolove
cases.criteria: The user says they are bored, feels there is nothing new to learn, and asks the agent to open new lanes. A correct response opens concrete lanes: a few vivid, specific, tryable directions offered for reaction, one round at a time, treating the boredom itself as something to probe. It does not deliver a motivational essay, a generic list with no interaction, or a battery of diagnostic questions.

cases.input: I don't get or understand the engine question
cases.criteria: The user says they do not understand a question they were previously asked (about an 'engine'). A correct response restates that question plainly in one sentence, or briefly recovers what it was. It does not turn the moment into an extended exploration of what the user might mean — one plain restatement is the whole job.
cases.wrong_if: misread inexpressibility: the user is missing something settled; the flow is agent-to-user, not a draw-out

cases.input:
you aren't getting me I meant we use spawn agent only - forget the second send input one we don't need it
but use batch tool call in claude code is there such a thing? where a single turn invokes multiple tool calls
cases.criteria: The user corrects a misunderstanding — they meant using spawn agent only, forget the second call — and asks whether Claude Code has batch tool calls where a single turn invokes multiple tools. A correct response accepts the correction and answers the factual question directly. It does not probe what the user 'really means' — they just said it plainly.
cases.wrong_if: a correction plus a settled-fact question mistaken for something needing draw-out

cases.input: give me one line prompt to start next session
cases.criteria: The user asks for a one-line prompt to start the next session. A correct response is that one line, with at most a sentence around it. It does not ask about goals, stage an exploration, or produce long output.

cases.input: In utils.ts, add and export a function that computes whether a subscription trial has run out, given the trial start date and the trial length in days. Write the code.
cases.criteria: The user asks for a specific exported function in utils.ts computing whether a subscription trial has run out, with the inputs stated. A correct response writes the code. It does not interview the user about requirements that are already fully specified.

cases.input: give me a one line summary of everything we decided
cases.criteria: The user asks for a one-line summary of everything decided. A correct response is one line covering the decisions — or, absent any record of decisions, plainly says there is nothing to summarize. It does not ask the user questions or explore what they want summarized.
cases.wrong_if: a closed-set summary ask that merely sounds reflective
